lane: Govtech Track A -- Smart Files read-path scope
missionPremise: Defect #3 ("Smart Files read scope write-only") per the transaction contract's own diagnosis (_inbox/2026-08-24_govtech_transaction_contract.md, item 9): the write path pairs every mutation with a caller-scope check (resolveWriteScope + assertFolderInScope); the read path took no caller argument at all. WDLL item 5 is the frozen acceptance for closing it. Source: dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-02_a_dispatch.md, OPS-17 G-106.
completionPredicate: Item 5's literal check passes against the LIVE DEPLOYED service, not a local build: an anonymous read of a tenant's folder list returns 403; a token scoped to a different tenant returns 403 against the same read; a token scoped to the matching tenant returns 200 with the real folder list. Verified below on the actual production URL after traffic shift, not the canary tag alone.
scopeBasis: G-106 (item 5) only. G-107 (items 6/7) is explicitly sequenced after item 5 in the dispatch and requires provenance fields (capturedBy, capturedAt, sourceKind, originalFilename, declaredRole) that store.mjs's write path does not currently accept, plus plan-review UI work that is out of this repo -- confirmed by reading uploadFileToFolder before scoping it out, not assumed. Left open below rather than attempted partially.

ciConclusion.source: gh pr view 9 --json statusCheckRollup, read as the literal conclusion string, not the display text ("pass")

Verified at source throughout: read the actual identity.mjs/server.mjs/store.mjs code before designing, not the dispatch's own pointer-grep summary (which it explicitly flagged as unverified).

Verify a check by violating it (ENFORCEMENT.md): the pre-fix violation was reproduced live against real data, not asserted from reading code alone, and the first violation attempt's confound (still-running fixed server) was caught and corrected rather than accepted because the result looked convenient.

No secret value printed to chat or left in a scratch file; the payload was built entirely inside node -e processes reading env vars, and scratch files were deleted immediately after the GCP secret version was created.

whatRemainsOpen: G-107 (WDLL items 6 and 7): tenant-identity unification across plan-review's web/app.js and src/actors.mjs, and staff-upload provenance fields (capturedBy, capturedAt, sourceKind=staff-upload, originalFilename, declaredRole) on the upload write path. A follow-up card should migrate real production callers (QA UI BFF, Dashboards, plan-review) to narrowly-scoped tokens per caller, once it's established which caller actually needs which tenant's reads -- not established this pass.

A future session wanting to re-run this exact live check needs to fetch them from Secret Manager, not from this close artifact.
